checks.label: For each 1.67 °C above 25 °C add one point (0.001) to the observed reading: a full cell reads 1.216 at 40 °C and 1.228 at 20 °C, and both correct to 1.225
A cell voltage of 2.10 V at room temperature means about 90 percent charge: the rested voltmeter reads 2.10 V at 90%, 1.96 V flat and 2.12 V full
Rest at least four hours, and makers recommend 24: the voltmeter reads 2.20 V just off charge, falls as it rests, settles by 4 h and reads the same at 24 h, and the rested tick waits for 4 h
As the charge falls, acid binds to the plates and the specific gravity gets lower: at every step down in charge the float sits lower and fewer acid dots stay in the liquid
The float reads 1.225 full, 1.213 at 90% and 1.105 flat, and the float and the voltmeter rise together as the charge goes up

High acid at the bottom makes the cell look more charged and raises its open-circuit voltage: stratified, the voltmeter reads higher than mixed at every charge, most acid dots sit low, and the hydrometer gives no reading
A low level reads 10 points high and an overfilled one 10 points low: a full cell reads 1.235 low, 1.225 right and 1.215 high, and its surface sits lower when low
The trust light says yes only when all four checks pass: rested, corrected, level right and mixed
Each puzzle accepts only its right answer, and nothing in its picture gives the answer before Check
Every demonstration settles within 4.6 s of its screen opening, and every answer's motion within 2.5 s
